paper.abstract_en: Magic captures nonstabilizerness, a resource required for quantum computational speedups. We prove the existence of multi-qubit nonstabilizer states from which no pure magic can be distilled, even with arbitrarily many copies and rounds of stabilizer operations. Such bound magic states have previously been only known to exist in odd Hilbert-space dimensions, where positivity of discrete Wigner functions can be used analogously to the positive partial transpose (PPT) criterion for bound entanglement. We introduce a PPT analogue for magic in multi-qubit systems that is closed under tensor products and stabilizer operations and reduces to the stabilizer polytope for one and two qubits. This enables the proof of multi-qubit bound magic and the explicit construction of bound magic states for $n \geq 3$ qubits.
